name: Saint Gregory the Great
history: A Roman aristocrat and city prefect who gave away his wealth to become a monk, Gregory was elected pope in 590 in a time of plague, flood and invasion. He fed the hungry of Rome, ordered the liturgy, wrote the Pastoral Rule and sent Augustine to convert the English. He called himself the servant of the servants of God.
life: Gregory was born around 540 into a senatorial family. After serving as prefect of Rome he turned his family house on the Caelian Hill into the monastery of Saint Andrew and lived there as a monk. Pope Pelagius II made him a deacon and sent him as envoy to Constantinople. Elected pope in 590, he accepted reluctantly and led penitential processions through the plague-struck city. With the empire weak, he organised food for the poor, negotiated with the Lombards and cared for churches in every region. Bede tells how he once saw fair-haired English boys for sale in Rome and said they were not Angles but angels. In 596 he sent Augustine and some forty monks to Kent. His writings on Job, on the Gospels and on the life of Saint Benedict shaped the faith of the Middle Ages. He died in 604 and is honoured as a Doctor of the Church and the apostle of the English.
prayerTo: Saint Gregory, apostle of the English, you sent missionaries to a far island and cared for the hungry at your door. Pray for the Church in this land, for our bishops and priests, and for me, that I may serve others humbly and bring to Christ those who do not yet know Him. Amen.
penance: Gregory organised food for the poor of Rome when the city was starving. Give to a food bank today, or share a meal with someone who would otherwise eat alone.
meditation: Gregory took the title servant of the servants of God, and every pope since has kept it. Whom are you called to serve today, rather than to be served by?
